# R336 — Quality evaluation for precision and residency-route changes

Date: 2026-10-13 (JST). Read-only review of current W source at HEAD 769ff3f11133a972bb9f7a78bb4a4cf52d52dcaf, R318/R289/R301/R331/R335, and SourceOnly fixed-history comparator v1. No project edits, tests, imports, builds, inference, GPU/profiler/process activity, Git changes, service checks, receipt/history changes, or cleanup. This report makes no quality claim about a candidate.

## Decision

Do not use exact generated-text equality as the universal quality gate. Exact greedy parity can be useful as a narrow deterministic-route regression signal: for a pinned build/device/input/config, a changed argmax reveals numerical or routing divergence worth localizing. It does not measure whether the candidate is better or worse in quality. Once one token differs, free-running trajectories diverge, so later text agreement is especially uninformative. Keep exact arithmetic microfixtures and any route-specific parity contract separate from model-quality acceptance.

For changing FP32 intermediate storage or residency/compute routes, the practical quality screen is paired fixed-history full-logit scoring plus a small held-out task suite. Calibrate baseline repeatability first. Report paired NLL deltas, full-distribution divergence and task outcomes with uncertainty; choose non-inferiority margins from intended product use and baseline variation before seeing candidate results. There is no defensible universal “zero degradation” cutoff for this model, precision boundary, device, or task.

## Relevant evidence and limits

- R318's three distinct evidence layers remain appropriate: exact microfixtures for arithmetic contracts; teacher-forced fixed-history comparisons for numerical drift; held-out tasks for quality. Operational faults and performance are separate. A/A repeat variation can inform the comparison, but cannot excuse NaN/Inf, missing rows, wrong positions, or a failed run.
- R331 establishes the current native standalone fixed-history row alignment: with prompt length P and N forced continuation tokens, row i predicts follow[i] at absolute position P-1+i. It also requires exact coverage, same token IDs and histories, complete finite full-vocabulary rows, successful lifecycle evidence and separate quiet performance runs.
- The Main-fixed-history-logits-comparator SourceOnly v1 can, by source contract, calculate float64 log-softmax, both KL directions, target log-probability/NLL deltas, ranks, top-two margins, top-1 agreement, quantiles and PPL with overflow represented explicitly. It rejects incomplete/misaligned artifacts rather than truncating to a common length. However, its packet says tests were not executed, no production receipt adapter currently proves the capture lifecycle/provider, and outputs always carry production_capture_qualified=false and quality_qualified=false. Therefore it is a planned analysis tool, not yet an available accepted quality result.
- Qwen Team's own Qwen3.8-Next report says candidate design changes are evaluated with loss plus downstream benchmarks and separately with prefill/decode cost; it explicitly observes that loss and downstream accuracy can diverge. This supports a layered assessment. Its reported model evaluations do not set acceptance margins for Strata's GGUF IQ3_S route or any Strata intermediate-storage change.
- The closest precision literature reviewed in R289 remains non-transferable: Qwen's qualitative FP8 GR-state statement is not a quantified Dm/GDN scratch result, and NVFP4 W4A4 results on Qwen3.8-27B are a different model and quantization boundary. Neither establishes an acceptable threshold for current Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S.
- Public evaluation guidance also separates fixed continuation likelihood from free generation and task scoring. EleutherAI's harness defines loglikelihood as scoring a continuation given a context and generate_until as free generation; its reproducibility paper emphasizes setup sensitivity and transparent evaluation details. This supports the methodology, not a numeric margin.

## Current route implications

The W source's current FP32 MoE Dm is read by moe_combine after each routed down projection. R335's accounting is 4*T*K*N bytes; with K=10,N=2,560, BF16/FP16 Dm would round each expert's down output before FP32 route-weighted combination. In the one eligible native fallback route, this is a per-layer rounding perturbation. A residency/compute route change can alter which kernel computes projections or how experts move, and may affect arithmetic even when persistent states remain FP32. These are numerical changes to score, not automatically quality loss. The exact candidate must declare whether it changes only residency/scheduling or also operation order, input format, accumulation, or storage; capture those route flags and per-layer route census in each arm.

A/A and A/B must pin the same model and GGUF shard hashes, tokenizer/template, prompt and continuation IDs, context positions, routing decisions, chunking, KV/GDN/PLE state policy, device/runtime/compiler, and all unrelated kernel settings. If routing itself changes, that is part of the treatment and should be retained in route-level evidence rather than silently described as a pure storage experiment.

## Smallest meaningful next experiment

1. Main first validates and executes the comparator's unit tests and reviews an adapter that derives receipt fields from actual successful, closed captures and source/provider evidence. No existing artifact should be marked qualified from the SourceOnly packet alone.
2. For a precision candidate, capture A/A baseline repeats and paired A/B fixed histories using the exact same token IDs. Start with at least one held-out 32K+ prompt history and a fixed continuation long enough to exercise repeated layers and chunk boundaries; for a compact screen, use multiple independent held-out documents so uncertainty is not inferred from a single long sample. Include shorter context only if the optimization affects it. Run capture arms separately from clean timing runs.
3. On the same fixed history, compare full-vocabulary logits and distributions at every covered position: paired target NLL/log-probability delta, mean and per-document NLL, forward/reverse KL distributions, top-1/top-2 and target-rank/margin summaries, and non-finite/saturation checks where applicable. Use paired document-level bootstrap intervals; preserve the per-sequence deltas. Fixed-history numbers diagnose whether the same histories are scored similarly; they do not replace task tests.
4. Add a small locked held-out suite matched to Strata users, with paired examples: deterministic code tasks graded by compilation/tests, exact long-context retrieval questions with known answers, and instruction/format/tool-call cases if those are in scope. Report each case and score delta, invalid-format/fault rate and an uncertainty interval. Increase example count until the predeclared non-inferiority margin is resolved or report the result as inconclusive. Do not substitute generated token equality for these outcomes.
5. Before inspecting candidate results, set margins for NLL and task scores based on intended use and the measured baseline A/A spread. If no product-level allowance is specified, report estimates and intervals without inventing a pass threshold. A candidate may be performance-promoted only after quality, numerical and operational gates have separately passed.

This is intentionally a screening sequence, not a universal sample-size recipe: corpus diversity, task variance, intended application and capture cost determine power. For a first Dm experiment, use one dtype at a time (BF16 and FP16 as separate arms) and do not combine it with a residency or kernel-order change. That isolates the cause of any measured difference. If the actual change is only expert copy scheduling with identical weight bytes and math, the same fixed-history check can confirm no numerical movement, while performance and operational measurements decide that optimization's value.

## Sources

- Qwen Team, On the Design of Qwen3.8-Next Architecture: Evaluation, Efficiency, and Training Stability (model-specific evaluation framing, not a Strata tolerance): https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.30320
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next official model card: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
- EleutherAI LM Evaluation Harness concepts, distinguishing log-likelihood and generation tasks: https://lm-evaluation-harness.readthedocs.io/getting_started/concepts/
- Biderman et al., Lessons from the Trenches on Reproducible Evaluation of Language Models: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14782
- Local policy/evidence consulted: R318, R289, R301, R331, R335; fixed-history comparator SourceOnly v1 contract at /home/yayoi/.local/state/strata-sycl/post-reboot-tuning-20261007/main-fixed-history-logits-comparator-source-v1/SOURCE_CONTRACT.txt.

## Limitations

No candidate output, baseline repeat, quality run, task score or comparator test was executed in this task. The official model report evaluates the BF16 model and architectural alternatives, not Dm16 or Strata's IQ3_S implementation. The SourceOnly comparator is not yet validated by main and is not a production-qualified capture path. No exact numeric non-inferiority threshold or sample count can be defended without product requirements and empirical A/A/task variance.
